The `pending → running` transition is a single conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'pending'` that stamps a timezone-aware UTC `started_at`, so of concurrent or repeated calls exactly one claims the job and any other — a concurrent loser, or a repeat call once the job has settled — returns `409 conflict` without changing state or writing an audit event. The winning run builds the existing read-only content export and settles exactly once: on success it returns `200` with `status: "succeeded"`, a timezone-aware UTC `finished_at`, `error: null`, and `result` equal to the body of `GET /v1/contents/{content_id}/export` (exactly `{"content", "claims"}`, claims for this content only in stable order each with its evidence bundles); if the export raises, it returns `200` with `status: "failed"`, a UTC `finished_at`, `result: null`, and `error: "content_export_failed"`. Either settlement records the `content_export_job.run` audit event in the same transaction, so the job is never left stuck in `running`. An unknown job id is `404 content_export_job_not_found`. Only the oldest pending job is claimed — every other pending job, including younger jobs, remains queued unchanged — and a second call then claims the next oldest. When no job is pending it returns `404 content_export_job_not_found` with zero writes (no job, resource, or audit row). The claim uses the same conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'pending'` as the single-job run, so of concurrent calls at most one wins any given job: a concurrent loser that picked the same oldest job before it was claimed gets `409 conflict` without modifying any job, creating any resource, or writing an audit event, and it never falls through to a younger queued job. The route never traverses lineage, changes the export snapshot's fields/order/UTC/error JSON, or alters job creation, detail, single-job run, idempotent retry, or `request_id` conflict semantics.
93	- `GET /v1/content-export-jobs/summary` — read-only queue summary over all existing content export jobs. The request body must be empty and the route accepts no query parameters: any non-empty body (including whitespace, malformed JSON, a JSON object, or any extra field) and any query parameter (unknown, blank, or repeated) is `422 validation_error`, and both validations complete before any job is read, so an invalid request never produces a partial summary. The success body is exactly `{"pending", "running", "succeeded", "failed", "oldest_pending_id", "oldest_pending_wait_seconds"}`: the four counts cover every existing job keyed by its current lifecycle state (settled jobs remain in their `succeeded`/`failed` counts), computed from the current persisted state at read time; `oldest_pending_id` is the stable id of the single oldest `pending` job in the stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic `seq` tiebreaker), and `oldest_pending_wait_seconds` is the current UTC instant minus that job's `created_at`, floored to whole integer seconds. On an empty queue every count is zero and both oldest-pending members are `null`. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON (compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII) terminated by exactly one newline; all numbers are integral (no `-0.0` or non-finite values). The summary is strictly read-only — success, empty results, and failures create no job, modify no resource, and write no audit event — and it freezes nothing: job status may change between reads, while the same persisted state read across an app restart returns the same counts and the same stable oldest id, with the wait time recomputed at each read's own instant. Job creation, detail, search, single-job run, queue claim, idempotent retry, `request_id` conflict, and export snapshot semantics are unchanged.

95	- `POST /v1/content-export-verifications` — stateless offline integrity verification of a received content export snapshot, for third-party verifiers. An empty `claims` list is a legal snapshot and the recomputed digest still covers that empty array. The snapshot is canonicalized under fixed rules (root member order and array element order kept, nested object keys sorted by Unicode code point, compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII, UTF-8) and hashed with SHA-256. A match returns `200` with exactly `{"valid": true}`; a structurally valid request whose recomputed digest differs returns `200` with exactly `{"valid": false, "computed_digest_hex": ...}`. Missing or extra top-level or nested fields, wrong member types, malformed JSON, a wrong algorithm, a malformed digest (uppercase, wrong length, non-hex, null, wrong type), an internally inconsistent snapshot (a claim on another content, a bundle attached to another claim), and any field carrying raw content bytes, a claim `payload`, evidence bytes, or a raw signature are all `422 validation_error` and never echo the submitted material. The route accepts no query parameters — any parameter is `422 validation_error`. It is purely a function of the request body: it never queries, creates, or modifies any resource, snapshot, audit record, or log, never saves raw material, and never traverses lineage, so unknown resources and repeated requests verify identically whether or not anything exists locally. The success body is compact UTF-8 JSON (compact separators, unescaped non-ASCII) terminated by exactly one newline; numbers stay integral (no `-0.0` or non-finite values). The existing content export fields, field order, UTC time format, error JSON structure, and persistence compatibility are unchanged.

97	## Verifiable attestations
98	
99	Attestations cryptographically bind an existing signing actor to an existing claim or evidence bundle. They only associate targets that already exist; they never create claims, bundles, or actors. The service verifies Ed25519 signatures but never holds a private key, and only verified attestations are ever written.
100	
101	- `POST /v1/attestations` — body contains `target_type` (`"claim"` or `"evidence_bundle"`), the existing `target_id`, an existing `signer_actor_id`, a Base64 Ed25519 `public_key` that decodes to exactly **32 bytes**, and a Base64 `signature` that decodes to exactly **64 bytes**. The signature is verified against the exact UTF-8 canonical JSON array (compact separators, non-ASCII emitted unescaped):
102	
103	  ```
104	  ["provenance-attestation-v1",target_type,target_id,signer_actor_id]
105	  ```
106	
107	  A signature over any other serialization (reordered elements, whitespace, ASCII `\u` escapes, a different prefix/actor) fails verification. The first creation returns `201` with the stable `att_` id, `target_type`/`target_id`, `signer_actor_id`, the Base64 public key, the `sha256` hex digest of the signature, `verified: true`, and a UTC `created_at`. The raw signature is never persisted or echoed — only its SHA-256 digest is stored. A repeat submission with the same target, signing actor, public key, and signature digest returns `200` with the existing attestation and writes no row or audit event.
108	- `GET /v1/attestations/{attestation_id}` — full public fields, or `404 attestation_not_found`.
109	- `GET /v1/attestations?target_type=...&target_id=...` — all attestations in stable creation order as `{"items", "count"}`, optionally filtered by `target_type` (`claim` / `evidence_bundle`; any other value is `422 validation_error`) and/or `target_id`. Filtering is an empty collection (`{"items": [], "count": 0}`), never a 404.
110	
111	The first attestation write and its `attestation.created` audit event commit in a single transaction. An unknown target is `404 claim_not_found` / `evidence_bundle_not_found` (matched by the declared `target_type`), and an unknown signing actor is `404 unknown_actor` even when the signature itself is valid. Bad Base64, wrong decoded lengths (32/64 bytes), blank identifiers, unknown `target_type`, undeclared fields, and malformed JSON are `422 validation_error`; a well-formed request whose signature fails verification is `422 attestation_verification_failed`, with no resource or audit write. Signature verification uses an RFC 8032 Ed25519 implementation in the Python standard library (no external crypto dependency).
112	
113	## Trust evaluation for reviewers
114	
115	Reviewers can ask the service to evaluate how many independent signing subjects have verified a given claim or evidence bundle. The evaluation is purely read-only: it computes its answer from the attestations already stored and creates neither a resource nor an audit event.
116	
117	- `GET /v1/trust-evaluations?target_type=claim|evidence_bundle&target_id=...&min_signers=...` — `target_type` is required and must be exactly `claim` or `evidence_bundle`; `target_id` is required and non-blank. `min_signers` is optional and must be a plain decimal integer from 1 to 100, defaulting to 1 (no sign, decimal point, or leading/trailing whitespace). Returns exactly `{"target_type", "target_id", "min_signers", "qualified_signer_count", "decision"}`. Only attestations of the exact target with `verified=true` and **no recorded revocation** are counted (every stored attestation is a verified one, but a revoked attestation is retained for history yet no longer qualifies), and the count is the number of **distinct** `signer_actor_id` values: several attestations by the same actor — for example under different keys — qualify once. If a signer's only attestation of the target is revoked, that actor drops out of the count; a target whose attestations are all revoked evaluates like one with no attestations. `decision` is `trusted` when `qualified_signer_count >= min_signers` and `untrusted` otherwise (an existing target with no qualifying attestations evaluates to zero signers and `untrusted`, not to a 404). The result is computed live on every request. Parameters are fully validated before any existence lookup: missing/blank/unknown/repeated `target_type` or `target_id`, a blank identifier, an undeclared parameter, and a non-integer, out-of-range, signed, or whitespace-bearing `min_signers` are all `422 validation_error` — nothing is silently defaulted or normalized. Once the parameters are valid, a missing target is `404 claim_not_found` or `404 evidence_bundle_not_found` according to the declared `target_type` (declaring an existing bundle's id as a claim, or vice versa, is likewise a 404).
118	
119	## Immutable attestation revocations
120	
121	A revocation is an immutable, append-only record that an existing attestation is no longer relied upon. It neither updates nor deletes the attestation: the original proof and its `attestation.created` audit relationship are preserved. There is deliberately no update or delete path for a revocation.
122	
123	- `POST /v1/attestation-revocations` — body contains the existing `attestation_id`, an existing `revoker_actor_id` (which need not be the attestation's signer), and a non-empty `reason` (surrounding whitespace is trimmed). The first creation returns `201` with the stable `rev_` id, the `attestation_id`/`revoker_actor_id` associations, the reason, and a UTC `created_at`. A repeat submission of the same attestation, revoking actor, and reason returns `200` with the existing record and adds no row or audit event; any different combination (a different revoker or a different reason) forms an independent record that is separately retained. Revocations never accept, store, or echo the original signature.
124	- `GET /v1/attestation-revocations/{revocation_id}` — full public fields, or `404 attestation_revocation_not_found`.
125	- `GET /v1/attestations/{attestation_id}/revocations` — that attestation's revocation records only, in stable creation order as `{"items", "count"}`; an unknown attestation id is `404 attestation_not_found` (a missing attestation is never an empty collection).
126	
127	The first revocation write and its `attestation.revoked` audit event commit in a single transaction. An unknown attestation is `404 attestation_not_found` and an unknown revoking actor is `404 unknown_actor`. Blank or whitespace-only `attestation_id`, `revoker_actor_id`, or `reason`, malformed JSON, and any undeclared request field are `422 validation_error` and write neither a record nor an audit event. Because records are append-only, any attempt to update or delete a revocation is met with `405 method_not_allowed`; no such mutation path is provided.
128	
129	## Read-only proof access grants
130	
131	A read-only access grant authorizes another actor to read one existing attestation through a protected endpoint. Grants are immutable and append-only: there is no update or delete path, and a grant never mutates the attestation it references.
132	
133	Both protected routes authenticate every request with three headers:
134	
135	- `X-PA` — the calling actor id;
136	- `X-PT` — the request timestamp as an RFC 3339 UTC instant (`Z` or an explicit `+00:00`; no naive or non-UTC value), no more than **300 seconds** from the server's current time;
137	- `X-PS` — a standard-Base64 Ed25519 signature (64 raw bytes) over the exact UTF-8 compact JSON array (compact separators, non-ASCII emitted unescaped):
138	
139	  ```
140	  ["provenance-access-v1",method,path,timestamp,body_sha256]
141	  ```
142	
143	  `method` is the uppercase HTTP method, `path` is the request path without any query string, `timestamp` is the exact `X-PT` header value, and `body_sha256` is the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the actual request body bytes — the digest of zero bytes for an empty (GET) body. The signature is accepted if it verifies under **any** public key of a non-revoked attestation created by the calling actor; a revoked attestation's key never authenticates.
144	
145	- `POST /v1/attestation-access-grants` — JSON body contains exactly `attestation_id` and `grantee_actor_id`; any undeclared field is rejected. Only the attestation's `signer_actor_id` (authenticated as above) may create a grant. The first creation returns `201` with exactly `{id, attestation_id, grantee_actor_id, created_at}` — a stable `aag_` id and a UTC `created_at`. A retried submission for the same `(attestation_id, grantee_actor_id)` pair returns `200` with the original record and writes no new row or audit event; a different grantee forms an independent, immutable record. The first grant write and its `attestation.access_granted` audit event commit in a single transaction. Missing credentials, an unparseable or out-of-window timestamp, malformed signature encoding, a signature no current key of the actor verifies, malformed fields or JSON, a missing attestation, a missing grantee actor, and a caller who is not the attestation's signer are all `422 validation_error`; no failure writes a resource or an audit event.
146	- `GET /v1/protected/attestations/{attestation_id}` — read-only. Only the attestation's `signer_actor_id` or an actor holding an access grant for that exact attestation may call it; success returns the existing attestation's public view (the same fields as `GET /v1/attestations/{id}`). A missing target, an unauthenticated caller, and an unauthorized caller all return the **same opaque `404 not_found`**, so existence is never revealed to a caller without access. An unparseable/out-of-window timestamp or a signature that is not canonical Base64 of exactly 64 bytes is `422 validation_error`. The read writes no resource and no audit event.
147	- `GET /v1/attestations/{attestation_id}/access-grants` — read-only, signed with the same `X-PA`/`X-PT`/`X-PS` contract over the empty GET body (the signed path carries no query string). Only the attestation's `signer_actor_id` may call it — a grantee who can read the protected proof cannot list its grants. A missing or unauthenticatable credential, a missing target, and a non-signer all return the **same opaque `404 not_found`**; an unparseable/out-of-window timestamp or a malformed signature is `422 validation_error`. Success is strictly `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}`; each item carries exactly `{id, attestation_id, grantee_actor_id, created_at}` in stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic sequence tiebreaker) and never echoes any revocation, private key, raw signature, authentication header, payload, or byte. Only `limit` and `cursor` are accepted: `limit` is a pure decimal integer in `1..100` (default `50`); any undeclared, repeated, blank/whitespace, or otherwise illegal parameter — and any malformed, unsigned, foreign-family, or non-binding cursor — is `422 validation_error`, checked before the target lookup. The opaque cursor is HMAC-signed and bound to the attestation, the authenticated caller, and the effective limit, so it resumes only the query that minted it; continuation pages repeat and omit nothing, the last page carries `next_cursor: null`, and a position past the tail returns `"items": []` with the same `count`. An attestation without grants returns an empty collection; the route is strictly read-only and leaves the existing grant and protected-read interfaces unchanged.

149	### Read-only tracking of grant revocations
150	
151	Reviewers can read the immutable grant-revocation records through two read-only routes. Neither route requires the `X-PA`/`X-PT`/`X-PS` headers, both accept **no query parameters** — any, blank, or repeated parameter is `422 validation_error` validated *before* the resource lookup — and both are strictly read-only: a successful read, an empty result, a missing resource, and a parameter failure create or modify no grant, revocation, other resource, or audit event.
152	
153	- `GET /v1/attestation-access-grant-revocations/{revocation_id}` — returns one existing revocation's public view, exactly `{id, grant_id, revoker_actor_id, reason, created_at}` with a UTC timestamp. The revocation id is the only lookup key — a grant id or attestation id is never reverse-resolved. An unknown id is an explicit `404 attestation_access_grant_revocation_not_found` carrying the requested `revocation_id` (an unknown id supplied together with a query parameter is the 422, since parameters are checked first). The view carries no private key, raw signature, authentication header, claim payload, content, or evidence byte.
154	- `GET /v1/attestation-access-grants/{grant_id}/revocations` — returns only that existing grant's revocation records as strictly `{"items", "count"}`, each item the exact five-field public view above, in the records' stable creation order (`created_at` with the monotonic sequence tiebreaker). The grant id is the sole lookup key — records are never resolved through a revoker, reason, attestation, or revocation id. An unknown grant is `422 validation_error` with `details.reason="grant_not_found"` (the same boundary as the revocation write route), never an empty collection and never a reverse lookup; an existing grant that has not been revoked returns `{"items": [], "count": 0}`. Repeated reads are deterministic and the views are unchanged across an app restart.
155	
156	## Content lineage relations
157	
158	Relations record how content identities descend from one another: `content_id` is the newer version or derived content, `parent_content_id` is its direct source, and `relation_type` is `version_of` or `derived_from`. Relations are immutable and append-only: there is no update or delete path.
159	
160	- `POST /v1/content-relations` — create a relation between two existing contents. The first creation returns `201` with the stable `rel_` id, both content ids, the relation type, and a UTC `created_at`; a repeat submission of the same three fields returns `200` with the existing relation and writes no row or audit event. An unknown content on either side is `404 content_not_found`; blank identifiers, an unknown relation type, a self-loop, or an edge that would close a lineage cycle are `422 validation_error` and write nothing.
161	- `GET /v1/content-relations/{relation_id}` — full public fields, or `404 content_relation_not_found`.
162	- `GET /v1/contents/{content_id}/relations` — the in- and out-edges of one content in stable creation order as `{"items", "count"}`; an unknown content id is `404 content_not_found`.
163	- `GET /v1/contents/{content_id}/lineage?direction=ancestors|descendants&max_depth=...&relation_type=...&min_depth=...&limit=...&cursor=...` — read-only multi-hop traversal. `direction` is required and must be exactly `ancestors` (content to direct source, following edges onward) or `descendants` (the reverse); `max_depth` is an optional integer from 1 to 32 defaulting to 8. Optional filters and paging: `relation_type` is exactly `version_of` or `derived_from` (absent means no edge-type filtering); `min_depth` is an integer from 1 to 32 defaulting to 1 and must not exceed the effective `max_depth`; `limit` is an integer from 1 to 100 defaulting to 50; `cursor` is an opaque server token returned by a previous page. Filtering only removes returned items — it never prunes traversal reachability, changes shortest-depth dedup, or changes depth/discovery ordering: an item matches `relation_type` when the edge through which it was *first* reached (at its shortest depth) has that type. Missing/blank/illegal `direction`, an empty/non-integer/out-of-range/repeated `max_depth`, `min_depth`, or `limit`, an unknown `relation_type`, a `min_depth` greater than `max_depth`, and an empty, malformed, tampered, expired-format, or query-parameter-mismatching `cursor` are all `422 validation_error` — nothing is defaulted or silently normalized, and no resource or audit row is written. The origin is never included; only contents reachable within the depth limit are returned, each deduplicated at its shortest depth, ordered by depth ascending and within a level by the discovering edge's stable creation order, as `{"items", "count", "next_cursor"}` where each item is the full public content view plus an integer `depth`. `count` is the total number of items after filtering, independent of the page returned; `next_cursor` is an opaque token for the next page or `null` on the final (and only, for an empty result) page. Re-sending a cursor with the same effective parameters resumes exactly where the previous page ended, with no duplicates or omissions; cursors are HMAC-signed and bind to the origin, direction, and every effective filter/limit value. No reachable contents yields an empty set. An unknown origin is `404 content_not_found`. The query reads only contents and relations (no resource or audit writes), deduplicates visited nodes, and terminates even if anomalous history contains a cycle.
164	
165	The first relation creation and its `content_relation.created` audit event commit in a single transaction.
166
